newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros premier jeered on visit to rebel island.
newsitem.headline: Comoros premier jeered on visit to rebel island.

text.p: The prime minister of the Indian Ocean Comoro islands was jeered on Saturday when he visited Anjouan island where at least two people were killed in clashes this week, witnesses said.
Residents of Anjouan demanding secession jeered premier Ahmed Abdou, an Anjouan native, when he visited the island under heavy military escort.
At least two people including one gendarme were killed on Monday on Anjouan in fighting between secessionists and security forces.
Secessionists, who want independence or a return to the French fold, hoisted French flags alongside the flag of a pre-independence sultan in defiance of authorities.
Opposition party leader Ahmed Abdallah Sambi, leader of the fundamentalist Front for National Justice, demanded on Friday an investigation into the killings.
The Comoro Islands has a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue independence has brought only poverty and civil strife.
